critic.claim: Re-run the peer survey with per-item counts, a very-disappointed question and a week-4 still-using question before building more.

One more round with counts replaces assumptions with stated numbers at near-zero build cost and gives the first product-market-fit read, which the product skills treat as the gate for growth work.

A very-disappointed share from a handful of peers means something. Next: print n beside every share and verify the threshold figure before asserting it, as product-discovery requires.
better_ways: Derive reach from operator-local receipts (weekly_receipt.py). Next: ask two operators whether they would share one; if neither will, the survey is the only route.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 5 peers answer within 14 days of sending: stop and keep ranking on assumed reach under the confidence cap.
The counts put any current top-5 item below 20 percent of respondents: re-rank from the counts before building that item.
critic.strongest_attack_survived: Self-selection and a small n make the counts unrepresentative. It survives because the item only replaces assumed reach with stated reach, keeps confidence capped until n is reported, and makes no fit claim below the stated n; the alternative, keeping assumed reach, is strictly weaker.

items.title: Benchmark the claimed differentiator (refusing to fabricate) with deterministic predicates, not a rubric judge
items.reach_src: assumed: operators of the opt-in product skills, plus how every prospect reads the positioning

items.risks: The predicates are heuristics tuned on Perun's own fixtures and could favour Perun; calibrate them on rival outputs first. A tie is a valid result and would retire honesty as the stated differentiator in positioning.
items.where: scripts/eval_predicates.py (bindings), the product skills' evals, docs/bench/ (a preregistration for the run).

critic.claim: Benchmark the claimed differentiator, refusing to fabricate, head to head with the deterministic predicates in scripts/eval_predicates.py instead of a rubric judge.
critic.steelman: Perun's stated differentiator is honesty and verification (docs/roadmap.md), yet its product-skill comparisons used model judges and no rubric-free pair beat a rival (H1c, H1d). Grading the one axis it claims with a deterministic grader removes judge and rubric bias and tests the claim itself.
assumptions: The predicates grade a rival skill's wording fairly; they were validated on golden pairs for Perun's own evals. Next: write 5 golden refusal and 5 golden fabrication outputs from rival runs and require the predicates to separate them before any scoring.
A rival skill can be run on the same bait prompts without its tools. Next: install one rival skill from its README and run one prompt end to end.
better_ways: Re-run the old pairs with a judge from another vendor (judge-independence-rerun). Next: price that second key; it still depends on a judge, so it stays a separate, lower-ranked item.
kill_criteria: The predicates fail to separate the rival golden pairs: stop, the instrument is not valid for rivals.
Perun and the best rival pass at the same rate (interval contains 0): drop honesty as the stated differentiator in positioning and do not widen the claim.
critic.strongest_attack_survived: The predicates are heuristics tuned on Perun's own fixtures, so they could favour Perun, the same bias class as the rubric. It survives only because done-when requires calibration on rival outputs and a pre-registered decision rule before scoring; without that step the verdict would be REVISE.
questions_parent_must_resolve: Is a small paid run (at least 20 prompts, two arms) acceptable? Next: the owner sets the cap; this pass runs nothing.
critic.user_question: May a small paid run, capped by you, test the honesty claim against one rival skill?
critic.dissent_ledger: Revised once: calibration on rival outputs and a pre-registered rule were added to done-when. The skeptic's bias point is accepted as the main risk.
critic.remaining_risk: The predicates stay narrower than real fabrication; a tie is a valid and useful result.

items.title: Cut review cost per unit of recall: ratchet the review path's tokens, then re-bench once
items.reach_src: assumed: every review run pays the cost
items.impact_src: docs/perun-vs-rivals.md#h7b-review-patch-only-the-real-skill-against-anthropic-toolkit-2026-10-16
items.effort_src: assumed: static budget rows, a reference-split pass, then a paid re-bench
items.vision_reason: Token optimisation and code review: review ties the cheapest rival on recall at about 3.5 times the cost, so cost is the measured gap to close. In the README run a review costs about $0.25 per unit of recall against $0.16 for a plain prompt (derived: cost per case divided by verifier-judged recall, 39 cases), and a rival's v6.4.1 added a cheaper execution mode (Native execution).
items.metric: Review cost per case at equal F1 vs the Anthropic toolkit: 3.5x ($0.0537 vs $0.0153, n=22, H7b) to 2x or less; web-archetype must-load ceiling 20,049 estimated tokens, ratcheted down.

adrs.title: Keep the flake ledger per host and untracked
adrs.context: train_flake.sh decides REAL or FLAKE per run with a same-host baseline file whose header it checks (a baseline from another host is refused), and it keeps no per-test history beyond that baseline. preflight.py already keeps a per-repo timing cache file meant to be gitignored (.preflight-times.json), so a per-host untracked store has precedent, and flakiness depends on the host.

options.name: Per-host untracked ledger beside the baseline
options.tradeoffs: Cheap, no merge conflicts, matches the same-host rule; each host learns its flakes separately.

options.name: Committed ledger file
options.tradeoffs: Shared across hosts and visible in review; conflicts on every train and records one host's flakes as facts.

options.name: Do nothing
options.tradeoffs: No new state; every run re-triages the same tests and keeps dropping PRs.

adrs.decision: We will keep the ledger per host and untracked, and print its quarantine list in the train summary, because train_flake.sh already refuses a baseline from another host and a committed file would conflict on every train.
adrs.consequences: Good: no shared state and no conflicts. Bad: each host re-learns flakes, and a quarantined test hides a real regression until its entry expires. Neutral: promotion to a committed skip list goes through an ordinary PR.
adrs.reversal_cost: Low, a two-way door: delete the file and the summary line; no other tool reads the format.

adrs.title: Compose the existing handback scripts in one thin entry point
adrs.context: A handback is six manual steps today (lane-preamble.md): wait, handback, clean_finished.sh, reap_own.sh, the changelog fragment and git diff --check. Each step already has a script and tests.

options.name: A thin script that calls the existing scripts in order and prints the cleanup
options.tradeoffs: No duplicated logic; one more entry point to keep in step with lane-preamble.md.

options.name: Grow lane_guard.py handback
options.tradeoffs: One entry point; mixes the start-of-lane guard and the end-of-lane automation in one file.

options.name: Do nothing, prose only
options.tradeoffs: No code; the survey (P7) still asks for automation.

adrs.decision: We will add a thin composer that calls the existing scripts and prints, never runs, the worktree cleanup and any base-branch fast-forward not covered by a human push grant, because every step already has a tested script and shared-state actions keep their human gate.
adrs.consequences: Good: fewer steps with no new gate logic. Bad: a second entry point to maintain. Neutral: dry run is the default, so the first release automates less than the survey asked for.
adrs.reversal_cost: Low: delete one file and its preamble line.

adrs.title: Enforce the background-work rule at the SubagentStop hook
adrs.context: lane-preamble.md says never end a turn with background jobs running, and the survey (P4) says lanes still do. handback_cap.py already blocks a handback while a git push from the worktree is live, by matching PUSH_RE against the process list and checking the cwd with lsof, but it matches nothing else.

options.name: Extend handback_cap.py's process check to any process with its cwd in the worktree
options.tradeoffs: Reuses a tested mechanism with its bounded wait and fail-open path; may hold a handback on a long-lived dev server.

options.name: Keep the rule in prose
options.tradeoffs: No code; it has not held (survey P4).

options.name: Register every background launch in a wrapper
options.tradeoffs: Exact, but needs a harness feature and touches every lane.

adrs.decision: We will extend the existing check to any process whose cwd is inside the worktree, with the same wait bound and the same COULD_NOT_CHECK fail-open path, because the hook already runs at the right moment and holds the cwd logic.
adrs.consequences: Good: closes the gap where the push check is already enforced. Bad: a user-owned dev server inside the worktree can hold a handback until the bound expires. Neutral: the nested-worktree bug in issue 1530 must be fixed first or together.
adrs.reversal_cost: Low: revert one function; no data or format is involved.

adrs.title: Store survey counts as an aggregate CSV in the repo
adrs.context: roadmap_rank.py reads each input's source as a path, a link or the word assumed, so measured reach needs a stable file that carries no personal data.

options.name: Aggregate CSV under docs/, counts and n only
options.tradeoffs: Versioned with the roadmap, reproducible and checkable by the privacy gate; no raw answers are kept.

options.name: Counts in an issue comment
options.tradeoffs: Easy to post; not versioned with the roadmap and lost if the tracker changes.

options.name: A form tool's dashboard
options.tradeoffs: Zero setup; third-party data that cannot be cited or re-derived from the repo.

adrs.decision: We will commit an aggregate CSV of counts and n only under docs/ and cite it from reach_src, because that keeps the roadmap reproducible and carries no names.
adrs.consequences: Good: measured reach is checkable in review. Bad: raw answers are not kept, so a question cannot be re-sliced later. Neutral: the form itself stays outside the repo.
adrs.reversal_cost: Low: the CSV is data; delete it and reach goes back to assumed.
